A brief pinned to an earlier head stays current when every commit after that head is a clean merge of the base: a merge commit whose second parent is an ancestor of the base, and whose tree (`git rev-parse <merge>^{tree}`) equals the one `git merge-tree --write-tree <merge>^1 <merge>^2` prints. The commits after a head are the branch's own, the ones `git rev-list --first-parent <that head>..<the current head>` lists; the base's commits come in through each merge's second parent. A runner makes such merges with no agent and leaves the brief as it was, so check each one yourself. A clean merge changes nothing the brief describes: judge the brief's evidence by this head's checks instead of its older pins. A merge whose tree differs carries a conflict resolution, which the brief covers like any other change.
